child_activity: Build a cushion fort together and read a book inside it.
Colour sorting: mix coloured blocks or bottle caps and sort them into bowls.
Water play: give {child} cups, a funnel and a tub of water; talk about full and empty.
Make a paper-plate mask of {child}'s favourite animal.
Treasure hunt: hide five toys and give simple clues ('under something soft').
Play-dough shapes: roll snakes, balls and letters of {child}'s name.
Sticker story: give a page of stickers and ask {child} to tell a story about them.
Bubble chase in the balcony or park; count how many {child} pops.
Kitchen helper: let {child} wash vegetables or tear lettuce.
Shadow puppets with a torch before bedtime.
Leaf rubbing: put a leaf under paper and colour over it with a crayon.
Dance freeze: play music and freeze when it stops.
Bath-time science: which toys float and which sink?
Make a 'feelings face' chart and ask {child} how they feel today.
Simple puzzle (6–12 pieces), letting {child} try before helping.
Draw with chalk on the floor or balcony; trace each other's hands.
Pretend shop: price toys with paper notes and play buyer and seller.
Sing action songs: 'Head, shoulders, knees and toes' or 'Machli jal ki rani hai'.
Fill a sensory bin with rice or dal and hide small toys to find.
Make a family photo book and name each person together.
Plant a seed (methi or mustard) in a cup and water it daily together.
Threading: big pasta or beads on a shoelace for fine-motor skills.
Animal walks: hop like a frog, waddle like a duck, crawl like a bear.
Mirror game: copy each other's faces and movements.
Clean-up race: who can put five toys away first?
learning_game: I spy with colours: 'I spy something red.'
Count stairs out loud each time you climb them.
Shape hunt: find three circles and three squares at home.
Rhyming game: cat, hat, bat… what else rhymes?
Opposites: big–small, hot–cold, up–down with actions.
Letter of the day: find things that start with today's letter.
Sorting laundry by colour or by family member.
Simple patterns with blocks: red, blue, red, blue… what's next?
Number line hopscotch with chalk, 1 to 10.
Name the sound: close your eyes and guess the noise (bell, clap, water).
Big and small: line up toys from smallest to biggest.
Two-language words: say the word in English and Hindi together.
Memory game with 6 picture cards face down.
Days of the week song while getting ready.
Count fruit at breakfast, then 'add one more'.
Follow two-step instructions: 'Pick up the ball and put it in the box.'
Weather watch: look outside and choose sunny, cloudy or rainy.
Body parts game: 'Touch your nose, now your elbow.'
Story sequencing: three pictures, put them in order.
Spot the difference between two drawings you make.
story: The Thirsty Crow: a crow drops pebbles in a pot to raise the water. Ask: what would you do?
The Lion and the Mouse: even the small can help the big. Ask: when did you help someone?
The Hare and the Tortoise: slow and steady wins. Race slowly together afterwards.
Make up a story where {child} is the hero who helps a lost puppy find home.
Ganesha and the race around the world: why parents are our whole world.
The Monkey and the Crocodile (Panchatantra): thinking calmly in danger.
Goldilocks and the Three Bears: practise 'too hot, too cold, just right'.
Tell the story of the day {child} was born, simply and warmly.
The Ant and the Grasshopper: why we prepare ahead.
Akbar and Birbal: the crooked line. Draw a line and make it shorter without erasing it.
A bedtime story about the moon visiting Bengaluru and looking at all the lights.
The Ugly Duckling: everyone grows in their own way.
Krishna and the butter pot: talk about honesty and saying sorry.
Make up a story using three toys {child} chooses.
The Little Red Hen: who helps, shares. Ask how {child} can help at home.
child_sport: Kick a soft ball back and forth 20 times.
Throw and catch a big soft ball from a short distance.
Balance walk along a line of tape on the floor.
Jumping practice: two feet together over a pillow.
Tricycle or balance-bike time in the park for 20 minutes.
Mini obstacle course: crawl under a table, step over cushions, run to the door.
Kids' yoga: tree pose, cat pose and butterfly pose for one minute each.
Swimming or splash-pool time with a parent within arm's reach.
Bowling with plastic bottles and a soft ball.
Running races in the park: 'ready, steady, go!'
Hopping on one foot, then the other, five times each.
Hit a balloon with a paper-plate racket to keep it in the air.
Climbing on a playground frame with you close by.
Dance to two favourite songs: it counts as exercise.
Walk the dog or walk to the shop instead of driving.
child_habit: Brush teeth twice a day for two minutes; sing a song to time it.
Wash hands before every meal and after the toilet.
Same bedtime every night; under-6s need about 10–13 hours including naps.
No screens during meals; talk about the day instead.
Keep screen time short and watch together; avoid screens in the hour before bed.
Offer water instead of juice between meals.
Let {child} put on shoes or clothes independently, even if slow.
Say 'please' and 'thank you' together at every meal.
Eat one new vegetable this week; offer it several times without pressure.
Daily outdoor time of at least an hour if possible.
Praise effort ('you tried so hard') more than results ('you're so clever').
Read together every night, even for 10 minutes.
Give two choices ('red cup or blue cup?') to build decision-making.
Practise a calm-down routine: three big breaths when upset.
family_activity: Family cooking night: make dosa or chapati together and let everyone shape one.
Evening walk together after dinner with no phones.
Board-game night: Snakes and Ladders or Ludo.
Gratitude round at dinner: each person shares one good thing about today.
Picnic on the balcony or living-room floor.
Family photo walk: everyone takes one photo of something beautiful.
Video call grandparents and let {child} show their drawing.
Make a family 'job chart' with stickers for small helpers.
Movie night with a short family film and home-made popcorn.
Paint pots or stones together and place them on the balcony.
Sunday clean-up: 20 minutes together, then a treat.
Fly a kite or play frisbee in the park.
Build something with old boxes: a car, a rocket or a house.
Visit the local library or a bookshop and choose one book each.
Make lemonade or nimbu pani together on a hot afternoon.
weekend: Lalbagh Botanical Garden: early morning walk and the glasshouse.
Cubbon Park on Sunday morning, when parts are closed to traffic.
Visvesvaraya Industrial and Technological Museum: hands-on science for kids.
Bannerghatta Biological Park: the butterfly park is a hit with toddlers.
Jawaharlal Nehru Planetarium: short shows suitable for young children.
Sankey Tank evening walk and duck watching.
HAL Heritage Centre and Aerospace Museum: planes up close.
Day trip to Nandi Hills for sunrise (leave very early, carry snacks).
Cubbon Park toy train and Bal Bhavan rides.
Weekend farmers' or organic market for a family breakfast.
Indoor play area or trampoline park on a rainy day.
Ulsoor Lake boating with life jackets.
Snow City or a kids' science centre for a hot afternoon.
Short drive to Muthyala Maduvu (Pearl Valley) for a nature walk.
Children's theatre or story-telling session at a local bookshop (check listings).
parenting: Get down to {child}'s eye level when giving instructions.
Name feelings: 'You're frustrated because the tower fell.' It helps them calm down.
Give a 5-minute warning before transitions like leaving the park.
Catch them being good and say exactly what you liked.
Model the behaviour you want; children copy far more than they listen.
Keep rules few, simple and consistent between both parents.
Offer limited choices to reduce power struggles.
Answer 'why' questions with curiosity: 'What do you think?'
Protect one-to-one time, even 10 minutes a day, with each child.
Keep calm during tantrums; safety first, talk later.
Let them struggle a little before helping; it builds persistence.
Routines reduce stress: same order for bath, story, sleep.
Limit sugar and screens before bedtime for better sleep.
Read picture books in both English and Hindi to build vocabulary.
Look after yourself; a rested parent is a patient parent.
